# Conclusion {#sec:conclusion}

The purpose of this report was to provide implementation-ready guidance for assigning NuSEDS escapement estimates to categories (Types 1-6) in a manner that is consistent, reproducible, and transparent to users. This objective was achieved by documenting a standardized decision framework that retains the existing classification structure while making the basis for each assignment explicit and auditable.

Specifically, the report establishes decision logic for Type assignment based on the principles outlined by Hyatt (Appendix E), clarifies evidence expectations for common operational complications, identifies the minimum metadata and documentation required to support transparent classifications, and provides standardized method roll-ups and mapping guidance to improve consistency in the interpretation of both current and legacy methods.

The framework does not replace professional judgement. Rather, it provides a common structure within which judgement can be applied consistently and documented transparently. Where evidence is insufficient to support a stronger classification, conservative downgrades are accompanied by standardized qualifier codes that clearly identify the reason for the decision and the information gaps involved.

Successful implementation will depend on routinely recording methods, key qualifiers, and supporting documentation during NuSEDS data submission and review. Consistent application of the framework, together with periodic re-evaluation as new information becomes available, will improve the transparency, reproducibility, and comparability of escapement estimate classifications across regions, programs, and years.

## Next steps

- Finalize a minimal, public-facing metadata schema for NuSEDS that supports the guidance (including quantitative uncertainty fields where available).
- Maintain a small set of worked examples (anonymized as needed) to demonstrate expected behavior in representative cases. Two examples are provided in this report.  
- Where possible, review historic estimates using the updated guidance.
